core_purpose: FlightLog is an open-source, Astro-powered changelog engine with a Linear-style dark-mode timeline UI for modern SaaS products. It renders MDX release notes from a content collection into a static, zero-JS site that can be deployed to Cloudflare, Vercel, or Netlify.

architecture.backend: None (static site; intended for Cloudflare Pages)

main_features.name: Scramjet AI Auto-publishing Pipeline (PR -> MDX commit)
Lint/Format Tooling (Biome + ESLint + Prettier + Husky + commitlint)

technical_debt: No automated test suite exists (no test runner, no test files, no test script in package.json). Tooling is duplicated and inconsistent — Biome, ESLint, and Prettier are all configured simultaneously, with lint-staged running Prettier while `npm run check` runs Biome format + ESLint. README contains an explicit `[TODO]` placeholder for a demo GIF and references a `.github/assets/demo.webp` that is not committed. The headline 'automated' Scramjet integration is described in prose only — no webhook handler, GitHub Action, or pipeline code is present in the repo, so the core 'Trojan Horse' value prop is documentation-only. External links (live demo at flightlog.scramjet.io, deploy-to-Cloudflare URL, Discord, scramjet.io) are unverified and may be aspirational. Astro 4.5 and @astrojs/check 0.5 are several majors behind current; pnpm is declared as packageManager but a husky/lint-staged setup still assumes npm-style flows.
active_roadmap: No open GitHub issues — roadmap is implicit. Likely next steps inferred from code: ship the Scramjet auto-publishing pipeline (currently README-only), add the missing demo.webp asset, consolidate the Biome/ESLint/Prettier toolchain, introduce a test suite, and upgrade Astro from 4.5 to current.
